summary:
Project title: Be An Earth System Trend Detective!
What problem are we solving?
Earth is continuously changing. Scientists collect enormous amounts of environmental data using satellites, Earth observation missions, and scientific models.
We'll create an Earth System Trend Detective Dashboard.
The user should be able to:
1. Select an Earth science variable.
2. Select a geographical region.
3. Select a time period.
4. Visualize historical data using interactive graphs.
5. Detect whether the variable is increasing or decreasing.
6. Calculate the magnitude of change.
7. Identify statistically significant trends.
8. View geographical patterns on a map.
9. Generate a report explaining the results

The application will distinguish between a trend that appears to exist and a trend supported by statistical evidence.
We'll also account for seasonality, missing observations, autocorrelation and multiple comparisons when analyzing real datasets.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective is a Python-based interactive dashboard built with Streamlit.

It helps users explore environmental trends over time using real environmental datasets from NASA POWER and NOAA.

Features

  • Environmental temperature trend analysis
  • Rainfall trend analysis
  • Soil moisture trend analysis
  • Global sea-level anomaly analysis
  • Interactive charts using Plotly
  • Statistical trend analysis
  • Year-range filtering
  • CSV data export

Data Sources

NASA POWER

Used for:

  • Temperature
  • Rainfall
  • Root-zone soil moisture

Representative locations:

  • Arctic – Longyearbyen, Norway
  • Amazon – Manaus, Brazil
  • India – Nagpur, India

Coverage: 2000–2025.

NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry

Used for:

  • Global mean sea-level anomaly

Coverage: 1992–2025.

Technologies Used

  • Python
  • Streamlit
  • Pandas
  • NumPy
  • Plotly
  • SciPy
  • PyMannKendall

Installation

Install Python, then clone or download this project.

Install the required packages:

pip install streamlit pandas numpy plotly scipy pymannkendall xarray netCDF4 requests statsmodels

Run the Application

Open a terminal in the project folder and execute:

streamlit run app.py

Scientific Limitations

  • NASA POWER values represent gridded data at selected representative coordinates, not regional averages.
  • Soil moisture represents root-zone wetness fraction.
  • NOAA values represent global mean sea-level anomalies, not absolute ocean depth.
  • The NOAA dataset does not include glacial isostatic adjustment correction.
  • Statistical trends describe historical patterns and do not guarantee future conditions.

Project Goal

To make environmental data exploration and trend detection accessible through an interactive dashboard
